request.prompt:
Identify the tool actually picked up by the hand named in the question. Images are chronological snapshots of one short recording, mixing whole-scene context and closer views. Time stamps use the original video clock. Several similar tools and printed pictures may be nearby.

Use the visible change between an earlier and a later image: a physical tool resting on the surface or being grasped, then the same object held off the surface or moving away with the hand. You do not need to see every intermediate instant. Check the final images before deciding that the hand only touched something. A nearby tool remaining on the table is not the picked object. A handled shaft supports screwdriver, a flat metal body with a wrench head supports wrench, and a hinged two-handle body supports pliers. Do not infer the tool's tip subtype, purpose, or correctness from the task.

Report brief observable facts, not reasoning. If identity or transition is unclear, use unknown/unclear. A tool already held throughout the images does not prove a pickup. Select before and after IDs from the supplied images, with before strictly earlier than after. The only valid IDs are context_0, target_0, target_3, target_6, target_9, target_12, target_15, context_3. Copy an exact ID; never output Picture 1, ordinal image numbers, timestamps, or a Frame prefix. Do not treat printed tool pictures as real tools.

Return JSON only:
{"tool":"screwdriver|wrench|pliers|unknown","shape":"handled_shaft|flat_wrench_body|hinged_handles|unclear","before_image_id":null,"before_state":"on_surface|grasping|already_held|unclear","after_image_id":null,"after_state":"held_away|on_surface|unclear","observation":"at most 30 words describing the same object's visible change"}
